from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and lecture lines for Section 1
        title_text = "Vectors as Physical Movements"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Start with a standard Cartesian coordinate system.",
            "Think of a vector as a movement through space.",
            "An arrow from the origin shows direction and distance."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        BLUE_COLOR = "#0000FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Step 1: Show a faint white (#FFFFFF) coordinate grid.
        # Origin (0,0) will be placed at D2.
        grid_plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": WHITE_COLOR,
                "stroke_width": 1,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.2
            }
        )
        self.place_at_grid(grid_plane, "D2")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR),
            Create(grid_plane)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Step 2: Think of a vector as a movement through space.
        # Robot starts at origin D2.
        robot = Circle(radius=0.15, color=WHITE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "D2")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR),
            FadeIn(robot)
        )
        
        # Animate robot moving 3 units right, then 2 units up.
        # Right 3: D2 (col 2) -> D5 (col 5)
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]), run_time=1)
        # Up 2: D5 (row 4) -> B5 (row 2)
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Step 3: An arrow from the origin shows direction and distance.
        # Draw bold blue (#0000FF) arrow from (0,0) to (3,2).
        vector_arrow = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B5"],
            buff=0,
            color=BLUE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Label the arrow '[3, 2]' in blue (#0000FF) at its tip.
        # Tip is at B5. Position label at B6 (within 1 grid unit).
        # Fix: Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' dependency error.
        label = Text("[3, 2]", color=BLUE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "B6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR),
            GrowArrow(vector_arrow)
        )
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup data
        title_str = "The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors"
        lecture_lines_str = [
            "Every 2D vector is built from two fundamental pieces.",
            "i-hat is a unit vector along the x-axis.",
            "j-hat is a unit vector along the y-axis.",
            "Combine these scaled pieces to reach any point.",
            "These basic building blocks are called basis vectors."
        ]
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_V = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines_str)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT))
        
        # Coordinate Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_I)
        )
        
        origin = plane.coords_to_point(0, 0)
        i_tip = plane.coords_to_point(1, 0)
        i_hat = Arrow(origin, i_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        i_hat_label = Text("î", color=COLOR_I, font_size=20)
        i_hat_label.next_to(i_hat, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), Write(i_hat_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_J)
        )
        
        j_tip = plane.coords_to_point(0, 1)
        j_hat = Arrow(origin, j_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        j_hat_label = Text("ĵ", color=COLOR_J, font_size=20)
        j_hat_label.next_to(j_hat, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(j_hat), Write(j_hat_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_V)
        )
        
        # Scaling i-hat by 3
        i_scaled_tip = plane.coords_to_point(3, 0)
        i_scaled = Arrow(origin, i_scaled_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        i_scaled_label = Text("3î", color=COLOR_I, font_size=20)
        i_scaled_label.next_to(i_scaled, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Scaling j-hat by -2
        j_scaled_tip = plane.coords_to_point(0, -2)
        j_scaled = Arrow(origin, j_scaled_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        j_scaled_label = Text("-2ĵ", color=COLOR_J, font_size=20)
        j_scaled_label.next_to(j_scaled, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat, i_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat_label, i_scaled_label),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat, j_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat_label, j_scaled_label)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Move j_scaled to tip of i_scaled
        shift_vector = i_scaled_tip - origin
        self.play(
            j_scaled.animate.shift(shift_vector),
            j_scaled_label.animate.shift(shift_vector)
        )
        
        # Resultant vector [3, -2]
        res_tip = plane.coords_to_point(3, -2)
        v_res = Arrow(origin, res_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_V, stroke_width=6)
        v_label = Text("v = 3î - 2ĵ", color=COLOR_V, font_size=20)
        v_label.next_to(v_res.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(v_res), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        basis_tag = Text("Basis Vectors", font_size=20, color=HIGHLIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_tag, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(i_scaled, color=COLOR_I),
            Indicate(j_scaled, color=COLOR_J),
            Write(basis_tag)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "Transformation: Morphing the Grid"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear transformations warp the entire grid of space.",
            "The origin must always stay fixed in place.",
            "All grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced."
        ]
        
        # Initialize the layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        GRID_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        ORIGIN_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        SQUARE_COLOR = BLUE_B
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Linear transformations warp the entire grid of space."
        
        # Construct grid lines (covering a local area)
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            # Vertical lines
            grid_lines.add(Line(np.array([i, -3, 0]), np.array([i, 3, 0]), color=GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=1.5))
            # Horizontal lines
            grid_lines.add(Line(np.array([-3, i, 0]), np.array([3, i, 0]), color=GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=1.5))
        
        # Central square (to show the warping effect clearly)
        square = Square(side_length=1, color=SQUARE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Group them for placement on the right-side grid
        visual_elements = VGroup(grid_lines, square)
        self.place_in_area(visual_elements, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Store initial center to act as our local origin (0,0)
        local_origin = visual_elements.get_center()
        
        # Animation: Highlight first line and show initial grid
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.play(
            Create(grid_lines),
            FadeIn(square),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "The origin must always stay fixed in place."
        
        # Highlight the fixed point (local center)
        origin_dot = Dot(point=local_origin, color=ORIGIN_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        
        # Animation: Highlight second line and show origin dot
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.play(FadeIn(origin_dot, scale=0.5))
        self.play(Flash(origin_dot, color=ORIGIN_COLOR, line_length=0.25))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "All grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced."
        
        # Define transformation matrix (Shear + Slight Stretch)
        # A 2x2 matrix for apply_matrix
        matrix = [[1.2, 0.8], [0, 1]]
        
        # Animation: Highlight third line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Perform the morphing transformation
        # We transform 'visual_elements' about the 'local_origin'
        self.play(
            visual_elements.animate.apply_matrix(matrix, about_point=local_origin),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Background and Title Setup
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        title = Text("Vector Space Visualization", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # 2. Lecture Content (Left Side)
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Definition of Basis",
            "- Linear Independence",
            "- Spanning Sets",
            "- Transformation Matrices"
        ]
        
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        lecture_vgroup.to_edge(LEFT, buff=1.0)
        
        # 3. Visualization Elements (Right Side)
        # Define a frame for the visualization on the right
        right_center = RIGHT * 3 + DOWN * 0.5
        
        square = Square(side_length=2.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        square.move_to(right_center + UP * 1.5)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        circle.move_to(right_center + DOWN * 1.5)
        
        # 4. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animate lecture points one by one
        for line in lecture_vgroup:
            self.play(FadeIn(line, shift=RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.8)
            
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animate geometric objects
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.play(square.animate.rotate(PI / 4).set_color(TEAL))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(circle, scale=0.5))
        self.play(circle.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5).set_fill(opacity=0.8))
        
        # Simultaneous animation
        self.play(
            square.animate.scale(0.8).shift(RIGHT * 0.5),
            circle.animate.scale(1.2).shift(UP * 0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Determinant: Scaling the Area",
            [
                "Determinants measure how much space is scaled.",
                "Look at the area of a single unit square.",
                "The transformation stretches or squishes this area.",
                "This area scaling factor is the determinant.",
                "A determinant of zero collapses space into a line."
            ]
        )

        # Local coordinate system helper
        # Origin at D2
        origin_pos = self.grid["D2"]
        def to_s(p):
            # Scale 0.5 to keep everything within A1-F6 right-side area
            return origin_pos + np.array([p[0]*0.5, p[1]*0.5, 0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Determinants measure how much space is scaled.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 4):
            grid_lines.add(Line(to_s([i, -2, 0]), to_s([i, 3, 0]), color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.3))
        for i in range(-2, 4):
            grid_lines.add(Line(to_s([-2, i, 0]), to_s([3, i, 0]), color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.3))
        
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Look at the area of a single unit square.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        
        # Gold 1x1 unit square
        unit_square = Polygon(
            to_s([0, 0, 0]), to_s([1, 0, 0]), to_s([1, 1, 0]), to_s([0, 1, 0]),
            color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color="#FFD700"
        )
        area_label_1 = Text("Area = 1", font_size=20, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(area_label_1, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        area_label_1.shift(UP * 0.3)

        self.play(Create(unit_square))
        self.play(Write(area_label_1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The transformation stretches or squishes this area.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE)
        )
        
        # Matrix M1 = [[2, 1], [0, 1.5]] -> Area = 3
        def m1(p):
            return [2*p[0] + p[1], 1.5*p[1], 0]

        para_poly = Polygon(
            to_s(m1([0, 0, 0])), to_s(m1([1, 0, 0])), to_s(m1([1, 1, 0])), to_s(m1([0, 1, 0])),
            color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color=BLUE
        )
        
        m1_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 4):
            m1_grid.add(Line(to_s(m1([i, -2, 0])), to_s(m1([i, 3, 0])), color=BLUE, stroke_opacity=0.3))
        for i in range(-2, 4):
            m1_grid.add(Line(to_s(m1([-2, i, 0])), to_s(m1([3, i, 0])), color=BLUE, stroke_opacity=0.3))

        self.play(
            Transform(unit_square, para_poly),
            Transform(grid_lines, m1_grid),
            FadeOut(area_label_1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This area scaling factor is the determinant.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        det_text = Text("det(A) = 3", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, "B4")
        
        area_label_3 = Text("Area = 3", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label_3, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Write(det_text), Write(area_label_3))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # A determinant of zero collapses space into a line.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(RED)
        )
        
        # Matrix M2 = [[1, 1], [1, 1]] -> Area = 0
        def m2(p):
            return [p[0] + p[1], p[0] + p[1], 0]

        flat_poly = Polygon(
            to_s(m2([0, 0, 0])), to_s(m2([1, 0, 0])), to_s(m2([1, 1, 0])), to_s(m2([0, 1, 0])),
            color=RED, fill_opacity=1.0, fill_color=RED
        )
        
        m2_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 4):
            m2_grid.add(Line(to_s(m2([i, -2, 0])), to_s(m2([i, 3, 0])), color=RED, stroke_opacity=0.6))
        for i in range(-2, 4):
            m2_grid.add(Line(to_s(m2([-2, i, 0])), to_s(m2([3, i, 0])), color=RED, stroke_opacity=0.6))

        det_zero = Text("det(A) = 0", font_size=32, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(det_zero, "B4")

        self.play(
            Transform(unit_square, flat_poly),
            Transform(grid_lines, m2_grid),
            Transform(det_text, det_zero),
            FadeOut(area_label_3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(Indicate(det_text, color=RED, scale_factor=1.3))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Seeing Space: Geometric Intuition in Linear Algebra
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students beginning Linear Algebra

sections.title: Vectors as Physical Movements
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite of the Cartesian coordinate system. Shift the perspective of a vector from a static 'list of numbers' to a dynamic 'arrow in space' representing displacement from the origin.
sections.example: A small robot character starts at (0,0). The vector [3, 2] is shown as an arrow pushing the robot 3 units right and 2 units up, emphasizing direction and magnitude.

sections.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
sections.content: Explain that all space is built from 'i-hat' (unit vector on x-axis) and 'j-hat' (unit vector on y-axis). Every vector is just a combination (linear combination) of these two fundamental building blocks.
sections.example: Visualizing i-hat as a red arrow (1,0) and j-hat as a green arrow (0,1). The vector [3, -2] is animated as '3 copies of red' and '-2 copies of green' being added together.

sections.title: Transformation: Morphing the Grid
sections.content: Introduce a Linear Transformation not as a formula, but as a 'warp' of space. Define the rules: the origin must remain fixed, and all grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced.
sections.example: A picture of a 'Square Cat' sitting on a standard grid. As a matrix is applied, the entire grid (and the cat) stretches and slants into a parallelogram shape, showing space itself morphing.

sections.title: Decoding the Matrix: Where do the Basis Vectors land?
sections.content: The 'Aha!' moment. Explain that the columns of a 2x2 matrix are simply the coordinates of where i-hat and j-hat landed after the transformation. This links the numbers directly to the visual change.
sections.example: A matrix [ [2, 1], [-1, 1] ]. We track the red arrow (i-hat) landing at (2, -1) and the green arrow (j-hat) landing at (1, 1). The 'new' space is instantly defined by these two landing spots.

sections.title: The Determinant: Scaling the Area
sections.content: Define the determinant geometrically. It is the factor by which areas are scaled during the transformation. If the area of a unit square becomes 6, the determinant is 6.
sections.example: A gold 1x1 square is shown before the transformation. After the space slants, the square becomes a larger parallelogram. The animation calculates the new area, showing how a determinant of 0 would 'squish' all of 2D space into a 1D line.

storyboard.title: Vectors as Physical Movements
lecture_lines: Start with a standard Cartesian coordinate system.
Think of a vector as a movement through space.
An arrow from the origin shows direction and distance.
animations: Fade in a faint white (#FFFFFF) coordinate grid on the black background.
Show a white (#FFFFFF) circle robot at the origin, then animate it moving 3 units right and 2 units up.
Draw a bold blue (#0000FF) arrow from (0,0) to (3,2) with a '[3, 2]' label in blue (#0000FF).

storyboard.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Every 2D vector is built from two fundamental pieces.
i-hat is a unit vector along the x-axis.
j-hat is a unit vector along the y-axis.
Combine these scaled pieces to reach any point.
These basic building blocks are called basis vectors.
animations: Show the origin with a faint white (#FFFFFF) grid in the background.
Draw a red (#FF0000) unit vector 'i-hat' from (0,0) to (1,0) along the x-axis.
Draw a green (#00FF00) unit vector 'j-hat' from (0,0) to (0,1) along the y-axis.
Scale red (#FF0000) i-hat 3x and green (#00FF00) j-hat -2x, then sum them tip-to-tail.
Flash the labels 'i-hat' (red #FF0000) and 'j-hat' (green #00FF00) to identify them as basis vectors.

storyboard.title: Transformation: Morphing the Grid
lecture_lines: Linear transformations warp the entire grid of space.
The origin must always stay fixed in place.
All grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced.
animations: Show a white (#FFFFFF) grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] and smoothly warp all lines into a slanted configuration.
Highlight the origin (0,0) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/origin.svg] with a yellow (#FFFF00) dot, keeping it stationary during the warp.
Pulse the slanted white (#FFFFFF) grid lines to show they remain parallel and equidistant.

storyboard.title: Decoding the Matrix: Where do the Basis Vectors land?
lecture_lines: A matrix tells us where basis vectors land.
The first column shows i-hat's new position.
The second column shows j-hat's new position.
These two landing spots define the transformed space.
Numbers in the matrix now have a geometric meaning.
animations: Display a 2x2 matrix [[2, 1], [-1, 1]] [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/matrix.svg] with column 1 in red (#FF0000) and column 2 in green (#00FF00).
Animate a red (#FF0000) vector i-hat moving from (1,0) to land at (2,-1).
Animate a green (#00FF00) vector j-hat moving from (0,1) to land at (1,1).
Warp the white (#FFFFFF) background grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] to align with these two new vector landing spots.
Highlight the matrix values while flashing the corresponding vector coordinates at their tips.

storyboard.title: The Determinant: Scaling the Area
lecture_lines: Determinants measure how much space is scaled.
Look at the area of a single unit square.
The transformation stretches or squishes this area.
This area scaling factor is the determinant.
A determinant of zero collapses space into a line.
animations: Fade in a white (#FFFFFF) coordinate grid on a black background.
Highlight a gold (#FFD700) 1x1 unit square with corners at (0,0) and (1,1).
Smoothly warp the grid so the gold (#FFD700) square transforms into a parallelogram.
Label the area of the gold (#FFD700) parallelogram as the 'determinant' value.
Flatten the entire grid into a single line and flash the determinant as '0'.
